text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: reserved-pool-usw2 CPU+NVMe pressure > 92% for 3m. 90% of requests delayed. Paging on-call: @mike_oncall

mike_oncall: grabbing it. seeing a spike from a customer batch job hitting /v1/generate-image; lots of long sequences.

kevin_prod: yep we're seeing a 6x RPS increase from tenant 'acme-data' starting ~09:02 UTC. Their backfill job spilled into prod routing.

mike_oncall: okay quick plan: 1) enable burst capacity on reserved-usw2 pool 2) apply temp per-tenant rate caps for heavy tenants 3) disable non-critical feature (image upscaling) if load persists.

oliver_platform: to toggle burst: run

```
rbctl pool toggle-burst --pool reserved-usw2 --enable --timeout 20m --reason "oncall surge mitigation"
```

mike_oncall: executing now. will also push QoS rate cap on tenants > 1k RPS:

```
rbctl qos set-tenant-rate --tenant acme-data --rps 250
rbctl qos set-tenant-rate --tenant thirdparty-ml --rps 200
```

incident-bot: Action logged: burst-enabled by mike_oncall at 1734509205.

elaine_support: prepping a short customer note for any tenants we throttle. I'll draft and post to #customer-impact for review.

sara_sre: taking secondary oncall for follow-ups. mike, want me to keep traffic shaping rules or revert if stable?

mike_oncall: handoff to @sara_sre in 5. I'll monitor next 10m and then hand over. If latency > 300ms persist, drop image-upscaling feature flag (ff-image-upscale=false).

kevin_prod: after burst toggle, CPU normalized to ~55% and queue depth dropped. RPS for acme-data reduced to 230. so far so good.

sara_sre: received. I'll keep burst engaged for max 20m per toggle and watch auto-scale counters. If we hit sustained >85% again, we'll extend burst 10m or engage emergency scale (ops approval).

mike_oncall: noted. Elaine, post comms: "We're investigating increased request volumes; temporary per-tenant caps may affect large background jobs. If you see degraded performance, open a support ticket and we'll advise."

elaine_support: posted and pinged affected customers. assigned follow-ups for ACME support case.

oliver_platform: adding a quick runbook note: "When toggling burst, also check KV cache hit-rate and evictions; aggressive burst can flush caches and cause second-order latency."

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated (burst enabled + tenant caps). Severity: S2. Logged runbook link: https://redwood/internal/runbooks/reserved-pool-burst.

sara_sre: I'm keeping the thread open and will update when we revert. thanks all. :thumbsup:
